paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Solomon lays two roads side by side all through this chapter, and every proverb is a signpost. One road is righteousness, and it ends in life, security and joy. The other is wickedness and foolishness, and it ends in ruin. Solomon never says the road is hidden, he just keeps pointing at it (Proverbs 10:16, 17).

Notice what keeps showing up on the way: hands, lips and mouths. "Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth" (Proverbs 10:4). "The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life" (Proverbs 10:11). What you DO and what you SAY are never small, because they carry you down one road or the other. And "love covers all transgressions" (Proverbs 10:12), so how you treat people is part of the road too.

Now here's the part that makes me grin. Solomon says "The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it" (Proverbs 10:22), and "The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright" (Proverbs 10:29). The road of wisdom isn't you grinding it out alone, it's you running into His shelter. So, baker, ask yourself which road your hands and your lips are on today, and then go on and walk in the way of the LORD.
